⬆️ Convective Clouds (Unstable Air)

Vertical Development
Towering Cumulus / Cumulus CongestusTCU
Cauliflower
Mod-Severe Turb Mod-Severe Icing Heavy Showers

"Cumulus clouds which are markedly sprouting and are often of great vertical extent; their bulging upper part frequently resembles a cauliflower."

CumulusCu
Mod-Severe Turb Mod-Severe Icing Heavy Showers

Fair weather puffy clouds with flat bases. Water droplets and ice crystals. Up and down drafts. Cold moist air over warm surface.

CumulonimbusCb
Severe Turb Severe Icing Hail / Thunderstorm

The thunderstorm cloud. Extends from low to tropopause. Can punch into stratosphere. Avoid by 20nm!

Cb CapillatusCb cap
Virga / Fibrous Top
Severe Turb Severe Icing Thunderstorm / Hail

"Cumulonimbus characterised by the presence, mostly in its upper portion, of distinct cirriform parts of clearly fibrous or striated structure, frequently having the form of an anvil, a plume or a vast, more or less disorderly mass of hair."

🌤️ Medium Level Clouds

6,500 - 23,000 ft
AltocumulusAc
Light-Mod Turb Light-Mod Icing

Mid-level puffy layer. Water droplets & ice crystals. Larger than Cc with visible shading.

Altocumulus CastellanusAc cast
Seen from side / Turrets
Light-Mod Turb Light-Mod Icing

"Clouds which present cumuliform protuberances in the form of turrets giving a crenellated appearance. The turrets are connected by a common base. The typical character is especially evident when the clouds are seen from the side."

Altocumulus LenticularisAc lent
Never touches ground / UFO / Lens
Mountain Wave Turb

Lens/UFO-shaped clouds in mountain waves. Appear stationary - air flows through while cloud stays in place. Indicates strong wind. Base: 7,000-18,000ft.

AltostratusAs
NOT Halo / Grey-Blue
Light-Mod Turb Light-Mod Icing Light-Mod Rain

"Greyish or bluish cloud sheet, totally or partly covering the sky, having parts thin enough to reveal the sun vaguely, as through ground glass. This genus does not show halo phenomena."

❄️ High Level Clouds

16,500 - 45,000 ft • Ice Crystals
CirrusCi
Narrow bands / Delicate filaments
No Icing No Turbulence

"Detached clouds in the form of white, delicate filaments or mostly white patches or narrow bands. These clouds have fibrous (hair-like) appearance, or a silky sheen, or both."

CirrocumulusCc
No Icing Light Turb

Small rounded puffs in long rows - "mackerel sky." Ice crystals. The ONLY high cloud with heap characteristics.

🌫️ Low Level Clouds (Stable Air)

0 - 6,500 ft
StratocumulusSc
Pebbles / Rollers
Light-Mod Turb Light-Mod Icing Drizzle

Grey/white patches, clear of ground. Water droplets. Base 1000-6500ft. Usually no precip but can indicate storms approaching.

NimbostratusNs
Often dark
Mod-Severe Turb Mod-Severe Icing Continuous Rain Poor Vis <20m

"Grey cloud layer, often dark, the appearance rendered diffuse by continuously falling rain or snow. Thick enough to blot out the sun. Low, ragged clouds frequently occur below."

💡 Lapse Rate Memory Trick - "Life Stability"

✅ STABLE Life

Expenses (ELR) < Salary (SALR)

Saving money → Air stays put

❌ UNSTABLE Life

Expenses (ELR) > Dollar (DALR)

Broke → Air keeps rising

⚖️ NEUTRAL Life

Expenses (ELR) = SALR or DALR

Breaking even

Isothermal: ELR = 0 → ELR < SALR (stable)
